title: Reviewer asks for gradient structure that permits SignMuon descent
detail: Explain a sufficient condition beyond the random-quadratic observation.
evidence: G1: aaai_article/signmuon_addendum_body.tex, conditional SignMuon theorem and geometry lemma; OLion v2, Lemma 4.3 / Corollary 4.4; exact-oracle, fixed-within-run momentum, uniformly positive margin.
finding: The diagonal-correlation condition implies alignment by weighting each diagonal entry by its nonnegative singular value. Uniform alignment, joint smoothness, centered finite-variance noise, exact polar and horizon-tuned fixed EMA/Nesterov yield an expected first-moment nuclear-gradient rate O(T^-1/4). It is a conditional result; actual trajectory verification and distributed-vote alignment remain open.
export_text: For momentum $M=U\Sigma V^\top$, if each diagonal entry of $U^\top\mathrm{sign}(UV^\top)V$ is at least $\delta>0$, then $\langle M,\mathrm{sign}(UV^\top)\rangle\ge\delta\|M\|_*$. A uniform margin, joint smoothness and unbiased finite-variance noise yield a conditional SignMuon rate; the margin is unmeasured in our networks.

title: Reviewer asks whether Theorem 4 includes decreasing learning rates
detail: Write the quantifiers and identify their limit.
evidence: N1: submitted Theorems 1–4 and proofs; aaai_article/ef21_signmuon_divergence.tex; evidence/verified_claims.json exact rational ascent/cycle certificates. Theorem 4 objective depends on fixed eta and mu; no decreasing-schedule impossibility follows. Only plain placements have one fixed softplus witness for all schedules; do not extend this to output EF21.
finding: For each fixed L, eta and mu there is an objective and either momentum variant diverges. The smooth objective may depend on those parameters. The scaled gradient floor is Omega(c_mu L eta), not a horizon-independent positive constant. No decreasing-schedule result is established for output EF.
export_text: Theorem 4 says $\forall L,\eta>0,\mu\in[0,1),\ \exists f_{L,\eta,\mu}$ causing divergence for the specified output-EF recursion with fixed parameters. It rules out universal constant-step rules based only on $L,\mu$. It does not cover decreasing schedules or rule out horizon-tuned finite-time rates: the objective depends on the parameters, and its gradient floor scales as $L\eta$.
